summary: Katrin Querl specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna and was attested in 2026 as a lecturer in Tibetan and scientific collaborator at the University of Hamburg.

Katsuhiko Kamimura (1944–2003) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Madras under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan, later serving as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo.

Katsuhiro Yoshizawa (born 1945) specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University from around 1964 to 1968 and served as a professor at Hanazono University around 1997.

Katsuji Fujioka (1872–1935) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Leipzig, later serving as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo from 1910 to 1933.
Katsumi Kuroita (1874–1946) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1893 to 1896 and held a post there from around 1901 to 1935.

Katsumi Mimaki (born 1947) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and in Paris under Gadjin Nagao, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Hisashi Sato, serving as a professor at Kyoto University from 1996 to 2010.

Katsumi Okimoto (1943–2014) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, directed the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (c. 2000–2009), and was a professor and professor emeritus at Hanazono University.

Katsumi Tanabe (born 1941) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and held posts at Kanazawa University (~1993–1999) and Chuo University (~1999–2012).

Katsutoshi Ono (1905–1988) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He earned his degrees from Kyoto University, held posts at Nara National Museum (1949–1967), and served as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1960–1980).

Kausthub Desikachar works in Indology and religious studies. He served as Executive Trustee of the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram until 2012 and founded both Viniyoga Singapore and the Krishnamacharya Healing and Yoga Foundation, where he serves as Chief Executive.

Kavita Singh (1964–2023) was an art historian and Indologist. She studied at Lady Shri Ram College, MSU Baroda, and Panjab University, later serving as dean at Jawaharlal Nehru University's School of Arts and Aesthetics starting in 2001.

Kazi Dawa Samdup (1868–1922) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ugyen Gyatso and Tshampa Norbu, served as headmaster of Bhutia Boarding School (~1906–1919), and became a lecturer at the University of Calcutta in 1920.

Kazu Uehara (1924–2017) specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyushu University, taught as a lecturer at the University of Miyazaki (1953–1968), and was professor emeritus at Seijo University (~1968–1995).

Kazuaki Komine (born 1947) works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned his degrees from Waseda University and served as an associate professor at Tokushima University and the National Institute of Japanese Literature before becoming professor emeritus at Rikkyo University.

Kazuaki Tanahashi (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Soichi Nakamura. He served as scholar-in-residence at the San Francisco Zen Center from 1977 to 1984 and is a fellow of the World Academy of Art and Science.

Kazufumi Oki (born 1946) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He served as an assistant professor (attested 1982–1988) and professor emeritus (attested 2006–2013) at Shuchiin University.

Kazuharu Mizuno (born 1958) is a scholar of Tibetology and geography. He studied at Nagoya University, Hokkaido University, and Tokyo Metropolitan University, and served as a geography professor at Kyoto University from around 2009 to 2024.

Kazuhiko Atsumi (1928–2019) was a scholar of philosophy and related fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1954) and held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1962–1989) and Suzuka University of Medical Science (~1991–2000).

Kazuhiko Yoshida (born 1955) works in linguistics, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sophia, Kyoto, Osaka, and Cornell universities under Jay Jasanoff and Teizo Iyanaga, serving as a professor at Kyoto University (~1996–2020).

Kazuhiro Kawasaki (born 1974) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his doctoral studies at Koyasan University, where he held posts as a researcher (attested 2005) and special appointment professor (attested 2026).
